title: Karna's abandonment
hook: asked who his father is, Karna has no royal answer; Duryodhana makes him a king, and an old charioteer walks into the arena
carry: it follows him into every room

segments.voice: Yesterday in Karna's abandonment, Karna matched Arjuna in the arena, and Kunti knew her son and kept silent — she can't tell anyone. Who in your crowd were you gentle with? Day seven hundred thirty-three.

Two fighters are ready to face each other. Then Kripa, one of the teachers, steps between them with a question that sounds polite. Arjuna is a prince, Kripa says, son of Pandu and Kunti. Tell us your mother and father, your royal line. A prince fights only an equal. And Karna, who has just matched every feat in the arena, has no answer to give. The text says he lowers his face. Here, on the last day of this part of the story, the abandonment comes due in public.
screen: `KRIPA ASKS FOR HIS LINEAGE.` → `A PRINCE FIGHTS ONLY AN EQUAL.` → `KARNA LOWERS HIS FACE.`

segments.voice: Duryodhana jumps in. If Arjuna will only fight a king, he says, then let Karna be a king. And there in the arena he has Karna crowned king of Anga. Karna, overwhelmed, asks what he can give in return. Duryodhana asks only for his friendship, and Karna gives it. Then, through the crowd, comes an old man, trembling, his cloth slipping. It's Adhiratha, the charioteer who pulled a basket from the river. And Karna, the new king, his hair still wet from the crowning, bows his head to him and greets him as his father. Adhiratha holds him and weeps. It's a beautiful moment, and it's the moment Bhima has been waiting for. You're a charioteer's son, he says, so pick up a whip. You're not fit to fight Arjuna, or to rule Anga. Duryodhana defends his friend: the origins of heroes, he says, like the sources of rivers, are hard to know. Look at the armor and earrings this man was born with. Then the sun sets, and the day ends with nothing settled. Look at the six days together. A girl's curiosity, a basket, a charioteer's home, an armor given away, a mother's silent recognition, and now a crown and an insult on the same afternoon. Karna's abandonment isn't one event. It follows him into every room. And the thing Kripa and Bhima hold against him, his birth, is the one thing he doesn't know the truth of.
screen: `DURYODHANA CROWNS HIM KING OF ANGA.` · `KARNA BOWS TO ADHIRATHA.` · `BHIMA: PICK UP A WHIP.` · `LIKE RIVERS, HARD TO TRACE.` · then, large: `IT FOLLOWS HIM INTO EVERY ROOM.`

segments.voice: Rest for two minutes with the breath. Bring to mind a time someone asked where you're from, or who your people are, and the question landed hard. Or a time you asked it of someone else. Just remember it. Then think of one thing you've done, not where you came from, that you're glad of. Let both sit side by side, the question and the deed. The bell holds the time.
Karna's abandonment. Asked his lineage, he lowers his face; crowned king, he bows to a charioteer; and the secret of his birth goes on following him.
Your line: it follows him into every room. Today, when you meet someone new, ask what they do or love before you ask where they're from. Day seven hundred thirty-three.

howItsDone: In retellings, Karna's bow to Adhiratha in the arena is told as a sign of his loyalty to the father who raised him, and his friendship with Duryodhana is traced to this day.

fork.setup: you're Karna, just crowned king. an old charioteer, trembling, comes through the crowd toward you. everyone is watching. what do you do?
options: bow your head and greet him as your father.
send a servant to lead him away.
fork.reveal: he bows to Adhiratha with his hair still wet from the crowning. it's the moment Bhima uses to mock him.

original.note: Sanskrit sūta: a charioteer; Bhima throws the word at Karna as an insult.

trapdoor: what you thought: Karna is made a king and the matter's settled.
what it means: the crown answers Kripa's question, but Bhima's insult shows the question of birth isn't going away.

what a scholar hears: Duryodhana points to the armor and earrings as signs of a high birth, and the listener knows he is more right than he can know; the fight itself never happens, because the sun sets.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva (Kripa asks Karna's lineage; Karna made king of Anga; Adhiratha enters; Bhima's taunt; Duryodhana's reply; sunset ends the day)
